items.followUp: Write four advantages of an electron microscope over a light microscope.

rubric.why: Electron microscopes can magnify much more than light microscopes.
rubric.description: States that an electron microscope provides higher magnification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its greater magnifying power.

rubric.why: Greater resolving power allows finer details to be distinguished.
rubric.description: Mentions the electron microscope’s resolving power or its ability to show finer details.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it can distinguish details that a light microscope cannot.

rubric.why: Electron microscopes can be used to observe objects too small to see with a light microscope, such as viruses.
rubric.description: Gives viruses or another suitable example of a very small object that can be observed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example.

rubric.why: Its magnification and resolution allow fine cellular structures to be studied.
rubric.description: Mentions observing fine cell structure or organelles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the study of cell ultrastructure or organelles.

modelAnswer: An electron microscope provides much higher magnification than a light microscope.
Its greater resolving power reveals finer details.
It can be used to observe very small objects such as viruses.
It shows the fine structure of cells and their organelles.

items.followUp: Briefly describe how Ronald Ross investigated the transmission of malaria.

rubric.why: Ross used sparrows infected with malaria in these experiments.
rubric.description: Identifies malaria-infected sparrows as part of Ross’s experimental work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the infected sparrows.

rubric.why: Finding malaria parasites in the mosquitoes provided evidence for mosquito transmission.
rubric.description: Reports the parasites found in the mosquitoes or the conclusion that mosquitoes transmit malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the experimental finding or its conclusion.

modelAnswer: Ronald Ross allowed mosquitoes to feed on sparrows infected with malaria.
He dissected the mosquitoes and observed malaria parasites in their stomach walls.
This showed that mosquitoes transmit malaria.

items.followUp: Explain how water movement in guard cells causes stomata to open and close.

rubric.why: An increase in guard-cell solutes draws water into the cells by osmosis, making them turgid and opening the stomata.
rubric.description: Explains how increased solute concentration leads to water uptake and opening of the stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the opening sequence: solutes increase, water enters, or guard cells become turgid and stomata open.

rubric.why: When guard cells lose solutes and water, they become flaccid and the stomata close.
rubric.description: Explains how solute and water loss leads to closure of the stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the closing sequence: solutes or water leave, guard cells become flaccid, or stomata close.

modelAnswer: When solute concentration in guard cells increases, water enters them by osmosis.
The guard cells become turgid and the stomata open.
When solutes and water leave, the guard cells become flaccid and the stomata close.
